text:
anya: FYI I opened a docs PR to consolidate rate/quota examples, standardize headers, and replace old dashboard links. The current pages had three slightly different code examples and the metering panels reference an outdated metric name.

sam: Drop the PR link? I can run a quick glance on the grafana queries.

anya: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5178 — it unifies the tier table, adds a short migration note for the metric rename, and provides canonical SDK snippets for header and sdk-opts.

mike: Are we explicitly modeling burst credits in the example or just showing effective steady rates? A few customers have asked for an explicit sample.

anya: I added both: a compact steady-rate table (S/M/L) and a small callout about burst credits consuming monthly allowance. Copy: "We provide steady-rate tiers and optional burst credits for short spikes. Burst credits consume quota.allowance and are not guaranteed throughput. Use quota.allowance_used to monitor consumption."

zane: For code, let's show both the raw header approach and the SDK-native option for Python + JS. Ops likes concrete requests examples.

anya: Added both. Examples in the PR: 

```python
# Example with requests + explicit header
import requests
resp = requests.post(
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/requests',
  headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY', 'X-Redwood-Client': 'docs-sample', 'X-Quota-Tier': 'pro'},
  json={'model':'rw-large', 'input':'Hello'}
)
print(resp.json())
```

```javascript
// Fetch example showing SDK option and header fallback
await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/requests', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`,
    'X-Redwood-Client': 'docs-sample',
    'X-Quota-Tier': 'pro'
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({model: 'rw-large', input: 'Hello'})
})
```

sam: LGTM on snippets. What metric rename did you document for the metering panels?

anya: Noted old -> new: `redwood.rate.tokens.total` becomes `redwood.token.count`. Example PromQL to replace existing panels: `sum(rate(redwood.token.count[5m])) by (model, tier)`.

sam: Can you add a one-liner sed/grep migration help so maintainers can bulk-fix dashboards in repo?

anya: Added: `git grep -l "redwood.rate.tokens.total" | xargs sed -i 's/redwood.rate.tokens.total/redwood.token.count/g'`

mike: Small nit: call out that historic dashboards may show gaps after the rename unless we create an alias or recording rule. Add a troubleshooting note about resampling/backfill.

anya: Added a troubleshooting section: create a recording rule or an alias in Prometheus during migration to avoid gaps, or run a one-off backfill/resample job. Example recording rule snippet included.

zane: Also linked SDK changelogs for header normalization (JS >= 3.2.0, python >= 1.5.0). I put a tiny compatibility table for customers to check versions.

deploy-bot: docs CI passed — 10 files changed, linkcheck OK, snippet tests OK. :white_check_mark: 

sam: I'll review the grafana snapshot changes once merged and then regenerate dashboards. Assigning @mike for copy review and @zane for SDK version verification.

anya: Thanks! If anyone spots other stray metric names or old dashboard links, please drop comments on the PR rather than pushing direct edits. Keeps the history tidy.

mike: One follow-up: add a short note on how burst credits show up in billing/export tables so customers can reconcile invoice rows with quota meters.

anya: Will add a short billing reconciliation FAQ entry before merge.

sam: Sounds good — target merge after two approvals.
